messages:
Priya: FYI brought up reranker-v3 (qat-lite) against v2-fp16 on two benchmarks: search-holdout-2025-01 and answers-bench-2024. Mixed signals: NDCG down ~0.4 overall but MRR up on answers-bench. Weird. Anyone free to quick-debug?
Liam: Can you paste the per-dataset numbers and cohort splits?
Priya: Paste:
```
dataset,metric,fp16,qat-lite,delta
search-holdout-2025-01,ndcg,0.542,0.538,-0.004
search-holdout-2025-01,mrr,0.312,0.306,-0.006
answers-bench-2024,ndcg,0.475,0.462,-0.013
answers-bench-2024,mrr,0.412,0.428,+0.016
```
Noah: So answers-bench MRR up but NDCG down. That suggests top-k ordering improves but rank distribution worsens (maybe more ties or score compression).
Yara: Could be calibration shift from QAT causing more confident top1 but worse tail. Do we have score histograms?
Priya: Quick histogram for answers-bench topk scores: mean_fp16=1.8 sd=0.9; mean_qat=1.6 sd=0.5 -> compressed scores.
Liam: Score compression fits quantization/QAT oddities. Another angle: dataset candidate composition differs (answers has many short docs). Any tokenization/truncation diffs?
Priya: I checked tokenizer version; both use tok v1.2.3. But export used different max_len: fp16 export used max_ctx=512, qat export accidentally used max_ctx=256 due to old export flag. That will truncate long context docs and could change doc features.
Noah: That mismatch could easily change NDCG on datasets with long passages. Does answers-bench have longer docs?
Priya: Yes median doc len answers=780 tokens, search-holdout median=120 tokens. So answers-bench is sensitive to ctx truncation.
Yara: Oof. So root cause might be export config mismatch, not quant technique. Suggest re-export qat with max_ctx=1024 and re-run. Also compare per-query topk overlap before/after.
Priya: Re-exporting now with `python export.py --model rerank-v3 --quant qat --max_ctx 1024 --seed 1` and will re-run eval.
Liam: Meanwhile add post-eval artifact that dumps for each query: fp16_top5_ids, qat_top5_ids, scores, and tokenized lengths. That makes triage easier.
Noah: Also run a small probe where we only quantize attention weights but keep FFN in fp16 (hybrid). If calibration is the issue, hybrid might keep NDCG while preserving MRR gains.
Priya: Good idea. I'll schedule 3 runs: (A) re-export full qat with max_ctx=1024, (B) hybrid-ffn-fp16, (C) ptq-perchannel baseline. Use bootstrap n=1500 for answers-bench slice.
Yara: I'll update the eval harness to fail if export max_ctx != expected for the model tag. We lost a guard there. Also adding a dataset-level sensitivity test in CI that compares anchor-run to new-run for truncation-sensitive datasets.
Liam: Quick ask: can we also compute pairwise MRR/ndcg flips so we get queries where top1 improved but overall ndcg dropped? That will help human triage.
Priya: Will attach flip CSVs to the job artifacts. Command: `./eval --model rerank-v3-qat --holdout answers-bench-2024 --dump-flips /artifacts/ev-1767777001/flips.csv`
eval-bot: queued jobs ev-1767777001-A,B,C; datasets=[answers-bench-2024,search-holdout-2025-01]; configs=[reexport-maxctx1024,hybrid-ffn-fp16,ptq-perchannel]; eta ~45m.
Noah: Action list in thread: 1) Re-export & re-run (Priya), 2) Add artifact dumps (Liam), 3) Hybrid probe + PTQ baseline (Priya), 4) CI guard for export ctx (Yara).
Priya: Will post results when jobs finish and attach flips + per-query artifacts. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
